headline: 7,500 Bangladeshis held in Saudi prisons, says State Minister Shama
summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam revealed the figure on Friday while receiving the body of a Bangladeshi national killed in Saudi Arabia.
details: Around 7,500 expatriate Bangladeshis are currently imprisoned in various cities across Saudi Arabia on various charges, according to State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam.
The State Minister disclosed this figure on Friday while speaking to reporters after the body of Shahed Ahmed, a Bangladeshi national killed in Saudi Arabia, was brought back to Dhaka.
Shama Obaed noted that Saudi authorities periodically provide lists of convicted Bangladeshis, but highlighted a lack of communication regarding some cases.
She specifically mentioned the execution of two nationals, Nazrul Islam and Sweety Akter, on October 14 over allegations of 'immoral acts' at a mosque in Makkah.
According to the State Minister, Bangladesh was not informed before the executions took place, and the Consulate in Jeddah has since requested copies of the verdicts from Saudi authorities.
While acknowledging Saudi Arabia's right to enforce its own laws, Shama stressed that the Bangladesh government should be notified when its nationals face such severe punishments.
She also questioned whether previous administrations had done enough to address these issues, noting that the case of the executed nationals dated back to 2023.
Additionally, the government is seeking visa extensions for Bangladeshis stranded due to conflicts in West Asia and exploring support for those who have lost their jobs.
caption:
Around 7,500 Bangladeshis are currently held in Saudi prisons.

Around 7,500 expatriate Bangladeshis are currently imprisoned in various cities across Saudi Arabia on various charges, according to State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam.

The State Minister disclosed this figure on Friday while speaking to reporters after the body of Shahed Ahmed, a Bangladeshi national killed in Saudi Arabia, was brought back to Dhaka.

Shama Obaed noted that Saudi authorities periodically provide lists of convicted Bangladeshis, but highlighted a lack of communication regarding some cases.

She specifically mentioned the execution of two nationals, Nazrul Islam and Sweety Akter, on October 14 over allegations of 'immoral acts' at a mosque in Makkah.

According to the State Minister, Bangladesh was not informed before the executions took place, and the Consulate in Jeddah has since requested copies of the verdicts from Saudi authorities.

While acknowledging Saudi Arabia's right to enforce its own laws, Shama stressed that the Bangladesh government should be notified when its nationals face such severe punishments.

She also questioned whether previous administrations had done enough to address these issues, noting that the case of the executed nationals dated back to 2023.

Additionally, the government is seeking visa extensions for Bangladeshis stranded due to conflicts in West Asia and exploring support for those who have lost their jobs.
